title: Seventeen Streets and One Shared Pump
subtitle: 社区与互助 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 社区与互助（社会服务与人际沟通·社区生活与互助）
meta: 主题语境：社区与互助（社会服务与人际沟通·社区生活与互助）　|　核心词汇：district　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 district 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1946 the alderman ① served a district that no councillor in the city would have chosen, and he said the serving was the whole of the term. The ② district, meaning the neighbourhood and not the division, ran seventeen streets and stayed unnamed on the plan; a district, he said, is the only thing in a city that is judged by how long it is left unvisited.

Every ③ district in that city had the same shared pump at the middle of it, and the ④ district at the end, meaning the one they kept for the new housing and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever inspected twice. A district, his clerk said, is nine parts walking and one part somebody willing to serve; the alderman said the walking is the part that fills seventeen streets.

The inspector meant the other thing entirely: she said ⑤ the district was the whole of the register, meaning the division and not the neighbourhood. The ⑥ district, meaning the division and not any of that, is the only thing in a register that everybody numbers and nobody visits; district, she said, is either something you serve or the only word that means both a neighbourhood and a division. She said the division is the part they remember.

By 1955 the ⑦ district had become a line in a list, and the list had become an argument about the shared pump. The ⑧ district of the whole thing, the alderman wrote in June, was one city and seventeen streets of walking; district, he said, is either the one at the end or the reason you learned to walk. She said the walking was never mentioned.

The ⑨ district I remember is the one at the end, which was renamed in 1969 and is still described as the quietest in the city. A ⑩ district, the clerk said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being visited; every district, she said, is a division that has agreed to look like a neighbourhood. She said the division was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 地区；街区（指城里有的那一片）
B. n. 街区（指那片社区本身，与那个行政区相对）
C. 固定搭配：serve a district 服务一个街区
D. n. 街区（指留给新建住宅用的那一片）
E. n. 街区；区域（抽象总称，指一座城市的街区之事）
F. n. 区（指名单上写到、被列名的那一片）
G. n. 行政区；分区（指登记簿上被编号的那个区划）
H. n. 行政区（抽象总称，指人人编号却无人到访的那个）

items.q: served a district that no councillor in the city would have chosen
The district, meaning the neighbourhood and not the division
the district was the whole of the register
the district had become a line in a list
The district of the whole thing
A district, the clerk said in 1971

answers.why: serve a district 意为“服务一个街区”，1946 年市政议员服务了一个全城没有一位议员肯选的街区。
district 意为“街区”，指那片社区本身而不是那个行政区，它涵盖十七条街道而在规划图上没有名字。
district 意为“地区、街区”，指那座城里每一片街区，每一片中间都有同一口共用的水泵。
district 意为“街区”，指留给新建住宅用的那一片，是唯一有人视察过两次的。
district 意为“行政区、分区”，指登记簿上被编号的那个区划，视察员说这个区划就是那份登记簿的全部。
district 意为“行政区”，指人人编号却无人到访的那个而不是那片社区本身，是登记簿里人人都编号、却无人到访的东西。
district 意为“区”，指名单上写到、被列名的那一片，到 1955 年这片街区成了名单里的一行。
district 意为“街区、区域”，市政议员六月写道，整件事的街区之事是一座城市和十七条街道的走访。
district 意为“街区”，我记得的是末尾那一片，1969 年改名，至今仍被说成城里最安静的一片。
district 为抽象总称，书记员 1971 年说，一片街区是唯一会因为被走访而变得更好的地方。
